pageCache.pageTitle: Blackheath High School | Independent Girls' School | GDST
pageCache.text:
a place Where girls boldly go
Welcome to Blackheath High School – a vibrant, forward-thinking school for girls aged 3-18.
We are on a mission to empower girls to dream big, think differently and achieve the extraordinary. Set in the heart of one of the world’s greatest cities, we are more than just a school – we’re a launchpad for future leaders, creatives, changemakers, and trailblazers.
We don’t just prepare girls for the world – we help them shape it.
An all-through school
designed for girls
We believe every girl should have the freedom to grow, lead and flourish in an environment designed entirely for her.
Here, there are no limits, no stereotypes and no barriers to ambition – just a community that empowers girls to find their voice and thrive.
Ours is a happy, diverse and dynamic community, rooted in academic excellence and enriched by a holistic education both in and beyond the classroom. Compassion, confidence and courage are at the heart of everything we do, in a school where individuality is celebrated and girls are encouraged to be fiercely and boldly themselves.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from our Head | Blackheath High School
pageCache.text:
welcome from our head
Natalie Argile, Head
I am extremely proud to be Head of Blackheath High School, a place where girls learn without limits. Empowered by the spirit of our pioneering feminist founders, this is a school where girls are free to discover who they are – in the classroom, on the sports field, in concert, or on the stage.
We combine outstanding academic results with a down-to-earth approach in a supportive environment, where every girl is valued and championed for who they are. We do this by knowing each student as an individual – her strengths, her skills and her ambitions; and by creating a community and culture where these skills are celebrated and encouraged.
The truth is that the world we’re preparing girls for is evolving faster than at any time in human history – many of the jobs our students will go into don’t exist yet, and most of the technology we use now will have moved on by the time they enter the workforce. It is our job to give them world-ready skills, and to prepare them with minds that are curious, adaptable, creative and forward-looking. Everything we do, from our curriculum to our Futures programme and PowerSkills toolkit, to our co-curricular and enrichment offers, is designed for their future as leaders and changemakers.
For us, leadership is more than a title. It is a mindset. It is a way of showing every girl, from Nursery to Sixth Form, how to use their voice, how to question and explore the world around her, and how to go forward boldly. With this approach comes empowerment.
Our most recent ISI inspection reflected what I see every day – confident, resilient, kind and ambitious girls thriving in an inclusive environment where every voice is heard and every talent is valued. This sentiment is further reinforced by independent reviews from the Good Schools Guide for both our Junior School and Senior School that “anything is possible”.
We are proud of our past and energised by our future, and we use this energy to empower the next generation of trailblazers.
It is a true honour to be Head of a school where girls boldly go.
Giving girls an outstanding start in life is at the heart of everything we do – and it’s what makes me so proud to be Head of Blackheath High Junior School.
Our education is designed specifically for girls, balancing academic excellence with creativity, wellbeing and an exceptional co-curricular life. From her very first day, each pupil is encouraged to find her voice, explore her passions and grow in confidence, guided by expert teachers who understand how girls learn best. It genuinely is a school where there are absolutely no limits on what girls can achieve.
Learning here reaches far beyond the classroom – from Forest School adventures and theatre performances to coding, sports and the inspiring Mighty Girls Challenge. Every experience helps our pupils discover new strengths and a lifelong love of learning.
What truly makes our school special, though, are the girls themselves – creative, kind, curious and full of courage. I feel so proud and privileged to be part of their world.
No website can fully capture the warmth, energy and joy that fill our school every day. I would love you to come and experience it for yourself – to meet our inspiring teachers, our bright, curious girls, and to see firsthand what makes this such a special place to learn and grow.
It is a privilege to lead the Sixth Form at Blackheath High – a place where individuality is celebrated, ambition is nurtured and every student is known, supported and inspired to achieve her best.
What makes our Sixth Form special is the balance of breadth and personalisation. We dream big for students, offering 25 A-levels options, the EPQ, and a wealth of leadership and co-curricular opportunities – yet we stay small enough for every student to be heard, valued and truly known.
Our future-focused teaching mirrors university learning, with seminar-style classes that encourage independence, creativity and debate. Students are supported by an expert team dedicated to their academic progress, wellbeing, university applications and personal growth.
Through leadership roles, enterprise projects and life-skills workshops, our Sixth Formers develop the confidence, curiosity and resilience to thrive wherever their journey leads next.
Most importantly, Sixth Form here feels like a true community. Students lift each other up, celebrate each another’s successes, and form lasting friendships with peers and teachers.
Every day, I feel proud to see our Sixth Formers grow into confident, capable young women, ready to take their next steps and shape the world ahead.
Blackheath High Nursery is where your daughter’s incredible learning journey begins. We know that the experiences, relationships and environment of these early years shape her future – so we make every day joyful, nurturing and full of discovery.
We’re passionate about helping pupils to feel challenged and to take risks in a safe, nurturing environment. In our small, happy classes, specialist Early Years teachers and experienced assistants create a space where girls feel confident to explore, create and grow. Through hands-on learning, imaginative play and outdoor adventures in our dedicated Forest School, they build curiosity, resilience and a lifelong love of learning.
From French, to PE, to Music, our specialist teaching from the very start ensures each girl is inspired, challenged and perfectly prepared for Reception and beyond – ready to take on every new opportunity with enthusiasm and joy.
We’d be delighted to welcome you to visit our Nursery and Forest School to see the magic in action.

pageCache.text:
staff & governors
leading by example
Blackheath High School leads by example. The culture of inspiration, innovation, passion and energy created by our leaders and teachers shapes students’ learning environment and experience.
The school is led by a Senior Leadership Team, and a Junior Leadership Team leads the Junior School. We also have a specialist Sixth Form Team, who are experts in the specific needs of Sixth Form students.

Junior Leadership Team

senior leadership team
With a background in Chemistry, Mrs Argile is a passionate Science educator with a particular interest in nurturing the creative side of the subject. She began her teaching career in a high-achieving comprehensive school in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, before moving south to teach in large grammar schools. She joined Blackheath High School in 2015 as a Deputy Head and Chemistry teacher, before being appointed Head in 2023.
An innovative leader and a passionate advocate of equality and education for girls, Mrs Argile is committed to ensuring every student reaches her own individual potential, whether that is through academic excellence, sporting achievement, creative endeavour or co-curricular interests.
Mrs Argile holds overall responsibility for the strategic leadership of Blackheath High School. She is committed to shaping and sharing a clear, values-driven vision and championing excellence in every area of school life.
Mrs Leamon began her teaching career in 1997, following university, as a Physical Education teacher at an all-girls school. A specialist in PE, she also developed a strong interest in teaching PSHE and soon discovered a deep passion for pastoral care. This led her to take on leadership roles as Head of Year and Assistant Head at a grammar school in Kent before joining Blackheath High School as Deputy Head (Wellbeing) in 2024.
Mrs Leamon holds strategic responsibility for pupil wellbeing, inclusion and engagement across the school. She leads the Pastoral Team in fostering and sustaining the school’s warm, inclusive environment; one where every individual is valued, supported and celebrated, and where inclusion thrives alongside aspiration and excellence.
With over 25 years’ experience in the independent education sector, Dr Drumm brings to Blackheath High a commitment to academic excellence, a bold, forward-looking vision, and a deep belief in the power of girls’ education.
As Deputy Head (Academic), Dr Drumm is responsible for the leadership, management and development of the academic life of the school. His role is to ensure the highest academic standards so that every student at Blackheath High can flourish and pursue her ambitions with confidence.
Dr Drumm holds a DPhil in Music Composition from the University of Sussex and an MA in Music and Education from the University of York. Before teaching, he worked at the Cabinet Office and for the Royal Collection. Outside of school, he is a keen cyclist and runner and enjoys hikes with his young family.
Ms Hickman is a passionate Geography teacher with a particular interest in political and economic Geography. She began her teaching career at a co-educational school in Buckinghamshire before moving to Thailand to teach at a leading international school in Bangkok. She joined Blackheath High School in 2017.
Ms Hickman is a strong advocate for civic engagement and believes in offering students meaningful opportunities beyond the academic curriculum. She values activities that enrich students’ lives, build a sense of purpose, and contribute to the wider community.
As Acting Assistant Head, Ms Hickman is responsible for overseeing progress and enrichment across the school. She works closely with the Deputy Head (Academic) to monitor and support student progress, ensuring each individual is able to reach their full potential. She also leads the development of a dynamic enrichment programme, equipping students with a broad range of skills to thrive in an ever-changing world.
I am Assistant Head of Pastoral at Blackheath High School. As a teacher of Physical Education and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead, I am passionate about our students’ wellbeing and holistic pastoral care.
My role is to ensure that students at Blackheath High receive a stimulating, rich and ambitious education – achieving their very best and being ready to leave school as informed and engaged global citizens.
I am committed to girls’ education, where every student is empowered to take risks to learn and grow.
Ms Cheyns is an enthusiastic and dedicated language teacher with a deep passion for girls’ education. Her teaching journey has spanned a range of educational settings, including nine years at a large grammar school for girls; an experience that solidified her commitment to empowering young women through education.
Driven by her belief in the importance of holistic development, Ms Cheyns is dedicated to equipping students not only with academic knowledge, but also with the skills and self-confidence they need to thrive in all areas of life.
As Head of Sixth Form, Ms Cheyns has overall responsibility for the strategic direction and day-to-day operations of the Sixth Form. Her primary focus is on delivering exceptional academic guidance and personalised pastoral care, ensuring that every student is fully supported and well-prepared for life beyond school.
Mr Ryan brings over 30 years of experience in Education Finance and Management, having worked across schools, Trusts, and Local Authority Education Departments. His extensive background includes overseeing multiple major school build projects, and delivering high-impact operational solutions. He holds a Diploma in School Business Management and is AAT qualified. With two daughters of his own, Mr Ryan is passionate about the mission and values of Blackheath High School, and is a strong advocate for girls’ education.
In his role, he provides strategic and operational leadership across the school’s business functions. He oversees administration, property management, health and safety, and financial operations, ensuring the smooth and effective running of the school’s infrastructure to support its educational vision.
Ms Fuell brings over 15 years of experience in advertising and marketing at Ogilvy, where she worked with a diverse portfolio of global brands including BT, BP, Ford, The Coca-Cola Company, Nestlé, and Unilever. Before joining Blackheath High School, she also worked for the Mayor of London, playing a key role in building the city’s international reputation. This breadth of experience has equipped her with the skills and insight to tell the Blackheath High story with creativity and impact.
Ms Fuell leads the school’s Marketing and Admissions team. She works in close partnership with the Head to bring the school’s vision to life, develop and deliver effective admissions strategies across all entry points, and foster strong relationships with alumnae and the wider community.
junior leadership team
With 24 years’ experience across independent, state, and international education settings, Ms Comerford brings a rich and diverse perspective to her role. She began her teaching career in co-educational primary schools before moving to a mixed international school. On returning to the UK, she took on a leadership position at an all-girls independent prep school – an experience that profoundly shaped her belief in the transformative power of girls’ education. She was inspired by how empowering it is to educate girls in environments where their voices are prioritised, their confidence is nurtured, and they are encouraged to believe in themselves and their futures.
As Head of the Junior School, Ms Comerford leads in close partnership with the Head of Blackheath High School. Her focus is on guiding, motivating, and inspiring both pupils and staff to achieve their very best, academically and personally, through a dynamic and challenging curriculum, a rich co-curricular programme, and exceptional pastoral care.
Ms Patel brings a unique blend of creative industry experience and educational expertise to her role. Before beginning her teaching career, she spent many years as a performer, theatre producer, and TV production manager. She then transitioned into education, gaining 15 years of experience in the state primary sector, where she developed a particular passion for literacy and drama. To deepen her understanding of leadership in education, she completed a master’s degree in Education.
Ms Patel works closely with the Head of Junior School to ensure that the curriculum is innovative, future-facing, and designed to develop critical thinking and a love of lifelong learning in every pupil. She oversees teaching and learning across the Junior School, manages assessment and reporting, and supports staff development to maintain the highest standards of educational practice.
With over 15 years of teaching experience in both independent and state schools, Ms Lucas has taught across both Key Stages 1 and 2, and brings a strong background in pastoral leadership. Since joining Blackheath High School in 2019, she has been instrumental in the development of the school’s bespoke Mighty Girls Challenge; a programme designed to foster resilience, creativity and problem-solving in pupils.
As Pastoral Deputy Head, Ms Lucas is responsible for ensuring the physical and emotional wellbeing of every child in the Junior School. She also oversees the development and delivery of a PSHE curriculum that is relevant, inclusive and responsive to the needs of the school community.
Miss Chandler brings 15 years of teaching experience across both state and independent schools, and has taught pupils from Reception through to Year 6. She has spent more than a decade working in Key Stage 1, giving her a strong understanding of each child’s learning journey – where they begin, how they develop and how best to prepare them for the next stage.
Her background also includes teaching in Special Educational Needs (SEN) settings, enabling her to support pupils with a wide range of additional needs. Through this expertise, Miss Chandler is able to guide parents effectively, signposting them to the appropriate support and resources to ensure their children receive the help they need.
Miss Chandler is passionate about empowering girls through education. She creates an environment that encourages exploration, creativity and curiosity, while intentionally nurturing early leadership skills. Her approach aims to equip girls with the confidence, independence, and resilience they need to become the leaders of tomorrow.
Miss Riordan has a degree in Primary Education & Art and 24 years of teaching experience across the state, international and independent sectors. She joined the GDST family in 2013 and moved to Blackheath High to take on the role of Head of Early Years four years later.
Ms Riordan is passionate about Early Years education as she believes it really is the most important and magical period in a child’s development. She is deeply committed to creating an environment where every girl feels confident, capable, and excited to learn, and is particularly inspired by the opportunities within the EYFS curriculum to challenge gender stereotypes and give girls the freedom to explore widely, follow their interests and truly be themselves.
In her spare time she enjoys exploring her creative side through sewing and other crafts, and volunteers with the Society of Bookbinders. She loves live music and chatting with her book group about their latest read.

Her professional work reflects a sustained commitment to educational innovation, creative leadership and student development. She is also the researcher and author of an Ofqual-accredited LAMDA Level 2 qualification in Speaking and Listening Skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nurturing a love of maths | Blackheath High School
pageCache.text:
Nurturing a love of maths
Our Nursery pupils have been busy exploring the exciting world of maths through hands-on activities, stories and play. They began by investigating 2D and 3D shapes, hunting for squares and rectangles around the classroom after enjoying Bear in a Square, before building with cubes, cylinders, spheres and prisms to discover which shapes could stack and which could roll. Along the way, they learnt new mathematical vocabulary including corners, sides, faces, edges and vertices.
More recently, the children have been developing their number skills through songs, practical resources and games. They have explored the concept of one more, one less and different ways of making numbers to five, confidently explaining their thinking using mathematical language such as add, equals and altogether. World Cup sticker collections have also provided a fun way to practise counting and adding goals together.
It has been wonderful to see the children’s confidence grow as they discover that maths is all around them and, above all, fun!

pageCache.pageTitle: Futures Programme | Blackheath High School GDST
pageCache.text:
futures
your future, your way
The Futures programme goes far beyond traditional careers advice. It is a pioneering, holistic framework that is built into the curriculum and supports every stage of each student’s journey with us, equipping them with the skills the World Economic Forum identifies as essential for future success in a fast-changing, digitally connected world. From the moment students join, they benefit from continuous skills development, tailored one-to-one guidance, leadership opportunities, inspiring workshops and world-class collaborations.
PowerSkills
Our PowerSkills Toolkit gives every Blackheath High girl the confidence and skills to thrive in a changing world. From leadership and collaboration to resilience, creativity and critical thinking, we focus on the attributes that future employers value most. As technology and AI transform the workplace, we also ensure students are equipped with the latest digital knowledge, so they can step boldly into the future as innovators, problem-solvers and leaders. For young women in particular, these skills are vital in a world where leadership is still unequal – empowering them to find their voice, claim their space, and lead with confidence.
World ready
GDST research shows that just 8% of girls nationally say that school prepares them for life, and nearly half (49%) say they feel unprepared for the future. They are also clear that being world-ready means more than just careers advice – it’s about looking beyond traditional, narrow definitions of leadership and success and helping them building confidence, curiosity and real-world skills.
Our Futures programme readies girls for how the world works and how to fearlessly carve their space within it. From managing money and budgeting, to online safety, engaging with different viewpoints and exploring current affairs, we equip every student with the knowledge, resilience and independence needed for life beyond school.
An all-through approach
The Futures framework begins from day one. Our youngest learners develop social skills, curiosity and early leadership through play and guided exploration. In the Junior School, co-curricular activities, collaborative projects, early STEM, our Future Forward careers event and the flagship Mighty Girls Challenge teach core skills, while building confidence and resilience and encouraging girls to try new skills.
By Senior School and Sixth Form, students take on advanced leadership roles, real-world problem-solving, internships and specialist workshops that prepare them for higher education and beyond. Alongside this, our careers programme, extensive events and one-to-one guidance give every student the chance to explore her passions, challenge assumptions about the world of work and imagine what her future could be. Working closely with families, employers and experts, we make sure each student leaves us confident, ambitious and excited for what comes next.
A networked world
Our extensive Sixth Form programme of careers events, visiting speaker days, student conferences, trips, workshops, partnerships and much more introduces students to a world of limitless opportunity, while teaching the value of connection and collaboration.
Through the Girls Day School Trust, we provide Sixth Formers with numerous opportunities to practise their future-facing skills, with initiatives such as the Space Technology Diploma – applying science, maths and computing to real-world space technologies; and GDST Lead – equipping them with the transferable skills needed to become future leaders and entrepreneurs.

our history
The Girls’ Public Day School Trust (GPTSD) is founded by four pioneering women – Mrs Maria Grey, her sister Miss Emily Shirreff, Lady Stanley of Alderley and Miss Mary Gurney – who strongly believe that girls should be entitled to the same academic education as their brothers. They enshrine the ethos that a GPDST education should be accessible to talented girls whatever their background, and offered scholarships from the outset – a principle which thrives at Blackheath High School to this day.
Rev. E Wilton South, Head Master of the Blackheath Proprietary Schools, calls a community meeting in Blackheath to draw up plans for a new public school – Blackheath High School. The meeting is attended by Mrs Grey and Miss Shirreff, along with Helen Taylor; a prominent suffragist who will eventually become the first governor of Blackheath High.
In the same year that primary education becomes compulsory, Blackheath High School opens its doors as the Girls’ Public Day School Trust’s first purpose-built school, on Wemyss Road. Designed for 300 pupils, the red-brick building offers half an acre of playgrounds, tennis courts and garden terraces, with elegant balustraded staircases still seen today in our Junior School. The school’s motto is "Knowledge no more a fountain sealed"; a reference to a new era of schooling for girls.
On 7 January 1880, HRH Princess Louise, daughter of Queen Victoria, formally opens the school, with Miss Sarah Allen-Olney as its first Headmistress. On 19 January, Margaret Robertson's name appears on the register as Blackheath High's first ever pupil. She is joined by 67 other girls studying English, Mathematics, French, Latin, Art, Needlework and Nature Study.
Florence Gadesden is appointed Head Mistress, a position she will hold for 33 years. A pioneering educator and passionate Suffragist, Miss Gadesden transforms Blackheath High – expanding the curriculum, introducing more opportunities for creative and physical expression, and championing the importance of sport for girls (including scandalously short sports skirts!).
Blackheath High Preparatory Department (otherwise knows as 'Stone House') opens at in 15 Montpelier Row. It later houses the Domestic Science Department – a kitchen and dress making room – and, eventually, the Sixth Form.
With the arrival of the Great War, girls are tasked with knitting clothes for servicemen and packing parcels of food. The school’s playing fields are turned into allotments.
Miss Gadesden retires, succeeded by Miss Gale, who builds on her pioneering legacy. Miss Gale oversees the addition of new netball and tennis courts, and the purchase of a Playing Field at Kidbrooke Park Road – an investment we still benefit from to this day as, over a century later, it remains the home of our inspiring floodlit Sports Campus.
Head Mistress Miss Lewis oversees the school’s evacuation to Tunbridge Wells High School, temporarily renamed Blackheath & Tunbridge Wells High School. In September 1940, the Wemyss Road building is taken over by the military – legend has it the special rooming system in the school today is a legacy of the Army’s time there.
Miss McCauley becomes Head and leads the school's return to Blackheath Village. Destruction is widespread but under her careful leadership, the Junior School swiftly reopens at 20 Montpelier Row, followed by the rest of the school back in its home at Wemyss Road. She also introduces the annual Gadesden public speaking competition, which is still in existence today.
Blackheath High becomes a Direct Grant School; a state-funded scheme to make outstanding education accessible to pupils from all backgrounds. Until the scheme’s closure in 1976, a quarter of Blackheath High’s students are on a Direct Grant place, fostering a diverse, ambitious and close-knit community – a spirit that endures today; our modern bursary programme is rooted in the same principles of philanthropy, inclusion and opportunity that have always defined Blackheath High.
Blackheath girls regularly achieve superb academic results. In 1960, one third of those going to university are admitted to Oxford, Cambridge and other leading universities – an extraordinary achievement given that women only began receiving Oxbridge degrees in 1920. This tradition of academic ambition and excellence continues today.
Guided by Head Mistress Miss Wheatley’s focus on the importance of civic duty and philanthropy, parents, staff and alumnae raise an incredible £30,000 to build a new gym. The school also introduces the annual ‘Senior Citizens' Party.
Mrs Williams is appointed Head Mistress and leads the school through its magnificent centenary celebrations two years later. A service of commemoration is held in Southwark Cathedral, and a tapestry is created by students and staff – it still hangs prominently in the school today.
Under the leadership of Miss Musgrave, the Senior School moves from Wemyss Road to a new site on Vanbrugh Park, formerly the Church Army Wilson Carlile Training College (opened in 1965). The Wemyss Road building becomes the exclusive home of our Junior School.
The Vanbrugh Park campus includes the striking Church Army Chapel, a listed modernist building designed by Ernest Trevor Spashett, which now serves as our Dance Studio.
With the new millennium comes a new Head, Lisa Laws. As well as developing and expanding the pastoral and co-curricular provision of the school, she also focuses on creating new facilities, including our purpose-built Theatre at the Senior School, and a floodlit AstroTurf pitch at the Sports Campus.
Overseen by Head Carol Chandler-Thomson, the Senior School completes its major £18m redevelopment, thoughtfully pairing elements of the old building with brand new, state-of-the-art facilities including light and airy Art studios, a new library, and the showstopping Louvre-inspired pyramid. The historic Datchelor stained glass panels, designed in 1896 and gifted by the Worshipful Company of Clothworkers to symbolise the school's heritage of pioneering education for women, are installed.
As part of our 140th anniversary and a year-long project devoted to sustainability and caring for our planet, the Junior School’s iconic stained-glass windows are installed. Entitled 'The Natural World', 'Community, History & Society' and 'She is Fierce' (chosen by pupils in homage to Shakespeare’s ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’), they powerfully reference our pioneering feminist spirit and re-imagine our historic Hall for a new generation.
Natalie Argile is appointed as Head, bringing with her an ambitious and future-focused vision with exceptional girls’ education at its heart, reflecting the pioneering spirit on which it was founded nearly 150 years ago. A year later, Laura Comerford joins as Head of the Junior School. Together, they are shaping the next chapter of Blackheath High, building on the school’s rich heritage and its bright future.

pageCache.text:
the nursery difference
Blackheath High Nursery is a magical place where your daughter will embark on a journey of discovery and growth, in an inspiring learning environment designed for girls. The early years of a child’s education are essential in all future learning – we provide girls with a joyful, enriching foundation to that future, supporting them to reach every milestone, achieve every ambition and learn without limits.
early years experts
Our small classes, expert Early Years teachers and dedicated teaching assistants ensure each girl receives the care and attention she needs to flourish.
Lessons in French, Music and PE with our specialist subject teachers mean that pupils benefit from high-quality teaching from the very start, laying the foundations for a lifelong love of learning.
Specialists in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework – which supports children’s development across key areas like communication, physical skills, literacy and maths – our teachers support girls to explore, discover and grow through hands-on learning in specially designed indoor and outdoor spaces, including our unique Forest School.
To meet our expert teachers and explore our amazing facilities, book a Nursery and Forest School tour.
academic and adventurous
Blackheath High Nursery offers a world of adventure and imagination; whether they are exploring our Forest School, building a fort, or making tea-time treats, our youngest girls develop independence, creativity and early academic skills through play-based exploration and discovery. Our highly skilled teachers understand that children learn best through curiosity, and that play is the most powerful learning tool – using a wide variety of teaching strategies to spark independent thinking and intellectual ambition.
a journey together
As part of the Blackheath High community, your daughter will be supported every step of the way, from her very first day in Nursery to Sixth Form and beyond. We go on a journey together. Our all-through school approach means we really get to know each girl – not just her academic progress but how she learns, what brings her joy, where she might need more of a challenge and what makes her thrive.
Without the pressure of the 11+ process to navigate, she can build lasting relationships, find her confidence and develop a genuine love of learning. Our consistently outstanding exam results are a testament to this approach, combining academic excellence with a deep commitment to personal growth, wellbeing and opportunity at every stage.
Start your daughter’s educational journey today!

Junior School Drama
imagine this
Drama plays a leading role at our Junior School. It inspires creativity, nurtures confidence and helps every pupil find their voice – whether in class, on stage, or in life.
From the many inspiring, imaginative play areas throughout the school, to the wealth of performance and speaking opportunities, Drama is woven into the fabric of our pupils’ learning.
specialist teaching
From Year 3 onwards, Drama is taught by a specialist teacher with lessons exploring a wide range of skills – from characterisation and improvisation, to performance, poetry and debate – encouraging pupils to think imaginatively, work collaboratively and perform with confidence.
Curtains up!
Performance is an integral part of life at Blackheath High. Throughout the year, pupils take to the stage in a wide range of productions that build skills such as confidence, creativity, leadership, collaboration, resilience and pride. From the heart-warming Nursery Christmas Play to the much-anticipated Year 6 productions – recent highlights include Olivia!, The Wizard of Oz and Kitty Whittington – every performance opportunity gives girls the chance to shine, grow and celebrate their achievements together.
opportunities beyond the classroom
Pupils can develop their love of performance through LAMDA lessons, Debating Club, and interschool competitions, as well as joint initiatives with our Senior School such as Shakespeare workshops, a Globe Theatre trip and a whole-school poetry competition.

JUNIOR SCHOOL MUSIC
music from the heart
Music plays a joyful role in life at Blackheath High Junior School. Whether it’s a choir rehearsal, a budding pianist practising, or a performance coming together, music is part of the rhythm of our days. We see music as more than a curriculum subject or a hobby – it is built into the school’s heart and soul.
A MUSICAL CURRICULUM FOR EVERYONE
We are passionate about helping girls to find their voices in everything we do, and this extends to our musical offering. Our inclusive curriculum is designed to allow girls to explore their musical interests and passions without any limitations or stereotypes.
Every year group from Nursery to Year 6 enjoys an hour-long weekly lesson with our specialist Head of Junior Music. Our primary Music curriculum encourages creative exploration through playing, singing, composing and listening, with each area thoughtfully interwoven to develop confident, curious and well-rounded musicians.
From Year 2 to Year 5, pupils’ musical learning is extended through small-group instrumental lessons, with instruments loaned free of charge for an entire term. This means that by the time they leave the Junior School, every girl will have had the opportunity to explore four different instruments, helping her discover where her musical interests and strengths lie.
CO-CURRICULAR OPPORTUNITIES
Co-curricular music is equally rich and rewarding, with non-selective choirs and orchestras alongside auditioned ensembles. Our Junior Chamber Choir is especially popular and has won several awards.
Individual instrumental and vocal teaching
A team of 16 visiting music teachers offers one-to-one tuition (available from Year 1 at an additional cost), covering a wide range of instruments including piano, drums, strings, brass, woodwind, voice, harp and more. Pupils who learn an instrument, either in or out of school, are warmly encouraged to perform in Junior School concerts throughout the year.
shining in the spotlight
Performance is central to music at Blackheath High Junior School, helping pupils build confidence, celebrate their achievements, and experience the joy of sharing their talents. From regular choir, orchestra and ensemble concerts, to ambitious stage productions, girls have countless opportunities to perform and grow.
her voice, her way
With specialist teaching and dedicated performance spaces – including our purpose-built Theatre at the Senior School – pupils quickly learn to find their own unique voice in front of an audience. Whether taking part in the Year 6 musical, joining voices at the GDST Sing concert, or representing the school in national competitions such as the Girls’ Schools Association Choir of the Year, every performance builds pride, confidence and lifelong memories. Each Christmas, our choirs fill the historic Old Royal Naval College Chapel in Greenwich with music – a truly magical highlight of the year.

A-level Results 2026
Blackheath High School A-level students celebrate another record-breaking year
84% of grades awarded A*-B
61% of grades awarded A*-A
A-LEVEL RESULTS
Blackheath High School is delighted to announce record-breaking results in 2026, with 61% of grades awarded A*-A, 84% of grades awarded A*-B and 17% awarded the highest A* grade. An outstanding 89% of students received an A* or A grade.
STEM pathways continue to be strong, with students progressing to study Medicine, Biomedicine, Medical Biosciences, Mathematics, Therapeutic Radiology, Environmental Geoscience and Product Design & Engineering, alongside Aeronautics and Astronautics, at leading universities across the country.
Mathematics students across the school excelled, with two girls achieving exceptional results ahead of schedule: Year 11 student Ellie achieved an A* at A-level, while Year 10 student Daisy secured an A in AS-level Maths.
Arts subjects also flourished, with Drama, Art, Design Technology, Textiles and Music awarded 80% A*-A grades, reflecting the strong creative culture of the school. Languages also achieved 100% A*-B grades.
An upwards trajectory
These results are the highest in the school’s history and represent an 89% relative increase since 2019, reflecting the highly aspirational academic environment fostered at Blackheath High School.
Head, Natalie Argile commented, “I am immensely proud of every single one of our remarkable students. These A-level results are testament to their ambition and determination, alongside the expertise, inspiration and unwavering support of their teachers. What really stands out is the extraordinary breadth of their achievements. There is no single definition of success at Blackheath High – we encourage every girl to find her own spark and give her the support, intellectual challenge and opportunities to pursue it. These students have worked incredibly hard for these fantastic results and are now heading in wonderfully different directions. Today, we are celebrating not only what they have achieved, but the confident, curious and bold young women they have become.”
Opening doors
Our students’ exceptional A-level results have opened doors to exciting new opportunities at some of the UK’s most prestigious universities and most competitive courses. Their journeys were supported by our enhanced Competitive Admissions Programme, offering personalised guidance for applications to selective universities and medicine-related pathways.
Top university destinations include:
Students will follow their own unique paths to study a hugely diverse range of subjects including Medicine, Biomedicine, Mathematics, Economics, History, Aeronautics and Astronautics, Therapeutic Radiology and Environmental Geographical Science.
University of Cambridge
University of Oxford
Pathways this year include:
Medicine – University of Oxford
History – University of Cambridge
Italian & Linguistics – University of Edinburgh
Psychology – University of Exeter
Aeronautics and Astronautics – Loughborough University
Fashion – Kingston School of Art
Medical BioSciences – Imperial College London
An outstanding year for EPQ
An outstanding 84% of Extended Project Qualifications were graded at A*-A. These independent research projects, equivalent to half an A-level, give students the opportunity to tackle topics they are passionate about, from researching scientific breakthroughs to creating short films or designing inventions.
This year’s topics ranged from an exploration of the lasting impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the NHS, a podcast on the importance of current affairs when teaching History to younger students, and a report into role of the UK media in shaping perceptions of Meghan Markle.
Natalie Argile continues, “It is inspiring to see students pursuing courses driven by genuine passion. The breadth of destinations reflects not only their academic strengths but also their courage to follow what excites them – something we wholeheartedly champion.
“Sixth Form and academic excellence remain central to our School Vision, and today’s results show the impact of this commitment. When students leave Blackheath High, they join the GDST alumnae network – a remarkable community of over 100,000 women. I know today’s achievements will propel them, and those who follow, to make an impact in whichever direction they choose.
“We are immensely grateful to our dedicated teachers and supportive parents, whose encouragement makes all the difference. As we celebrate these results, we look forward to seeing our students thrive in higher education and beyond, and to nurturing the next generation of thinkers, creators and trailblazers.”
Read about some of our fantastic students and their stories of success at Blackheath High School:
Gloria – a passion for Medicine
Gloria joined her two older sisters at Blackheath High School, entering Year 7 from Fairlawn Primary School. Drawn by its friendly atmosphere, strong sense of academic ambition and small class sizes which allowed for closer relationships with teachers, she quickly felt like she had found her home.
Following outstanding A-level results – A* Biology and Chemistry and A in Maths and Spanish, Gloria will take up her place at St Catherine’s College, Oxford, to study Medicine, with the ambition of one day becoming a neonatal paediatric consultant. She also achieved an A* in her EPQ, which explored the lasting impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the NHS.
Embracing every challenge
An Academic Scholar, Gloria consistently challenges herself, winning a prestigious Gold CREST Award for her EPQ, receiving a Gold Award in the Cambridge Chemistry Challenge, Silver Awards in both the UK Chemistry Olympiad and Intermediate Biology Olympiad, and completing many piano grade exams.
Her life beyond the classroom has been equally busy. Throughout her time at Blackheath High, Gloria has sung with Chamber Choir, The Rollin’ Tones and Vocalise; supported younger students as a Peer Mentor, Year 7 Prefect and Head of Paragon House; and nurtured her passion for science as Chemistry Subject Prefect, founder of Dissection Society and co-leader of First Aid Society.
Gloria credits Blackheath High with nurturing her passion for Medicine. Alongside the school’s bespoke competitive admissions programme, she attended the GDST Oxbridge Conference at Clare College, Cambridge, where she gained invaluable insight into university life.
She says, “it was one of the most impactful things I have ever done. The Medicine-specific talks gave me advice on preparing for the UCAT and I got to take part in a mock Case-Based Learning session, which is the type of teaching used in most medical schools – which then gave me content for my personal statement. It was an incredible insight into university life.”
Looking to the future
Gloria loved her Sixth Form experience, where she truly found her path. “The teachers are one of the best things about Blackheath High – they are so approachable and they were all willing to support me with my Medicine interviews, giving up their free time to help me – I will never forget that.
“I love the more relaxed style of teaching and the close-knit classes, which foster a close-knit and interactive environment. And I feel like Sixth Form helped me with some many life skills – teamwork, organisation skills, leadership, communication, budgeting and learning how to take constructive feedback and build on it.”
Ananya – Future Economist
Joining Blackheath High in Year 7 from Gatehouse School, Ananya was drawn by the school’s outstanding Art department and inspired by the positive experiences of her older sister, who was two years above her. Six years later, she leaves with A grades in History and Economics, and an A* in Art, alongside an A-graded EPQ exploring the role of the UK media in shaping public perceptions of Meghan Markle.
Ananya leaves us to study Economics at the University of Sheffield, attracted by the subject’s relevance to the world around us and the opportunity to apply economic thinking to real-life issues. Her EPQ also helped prepare her for the academic challenges of university study, as it required independence, motivation and discipline.
Making the most of every opportunity
Ananya has embraced many of the opportunities Blackheath High has to offer over her time here. An Art Scholar and recipient of the Lucy Forrest Art Scholarship, she was also an Art Subject Prefect in Year 12 and played guitar in Rock Band until Year 11. She has proudly represented the school in netball, completed both Bronze and Silver Duke of Edinburgh’s Awards, and spent many happy hours supporting younger pupils at the Junior School After School Club.
Reflecting on Sixth Form, Ananya says some of her happiest memories were made in the close-knit community, whether playing sport or spending time with friends in the common room as everyone planned their next steps. “I really like that Blackheath High is a smaller school because people know you well, especially in Sixth Form. It’s a place where individuality is encouraged and listened to, and that’s helped me grow in confidence and prepare for what’s next.”
Preparing for the future
Thinking about the teaching style, Ananya particularly appreciated the discussion-based teaching and small-group learning style “which allow for debate and deeper thinking when you’re thinking about new concepts and information – really important as get to grips with the move from GCSE to A-level.
“I also didn’t realise how much I would value the way Blackheath High gives us so many life skills to use in our future lives such as learning basic car maintenance, cooking skills and financial literacy. I feel more prepared for life beyond school now.”
Eva – a passion for global development
Eva joined Blackheath High in Year 3 from River House Montessori School. From her very first taster day, she remembers feeling welcomed and at home in the school community.
Now, after receiving A grades in Geography and Textiles at A-level, a B in Biology and an A for her EPQ exploring the question ‘Should volcano tourism be banned?’, Eva will be taking up a place at the University of Manchester to study Human Geography. With a particular interest in social inequality, global development and geopolitics, she hopes eventually to pursue a career where she can make a difference, ideally in global development or international relations.
Discovering new passions
Eva has made the most of the many opportunities to explore her passions. A keen netball player, she continued playing throughout Sixth Form, valuing the chance to enjoy sport and spend time with friends beyond the classroom. She also discovered her passion for Textiles and garment-making when she joined Fashion Society in Year 9. Inspired to take the subject at A-level, she went on to design and create her own final collection and take part in the prestigious Fashion Show, working with models from Years 7 to 13.
Eva has also supported younger pupils as Senior Prefect, listening to their ideas about school life and representing their views.
A new perspective on the world
One of the defining experiences of Eva’s time at Blackheath High happed in the summer of 2024 when she spent four weeks with fellow students on an expedition to Peru, taking part in community projects, learning about local culture and completing a five-day trek to Machu Picchu.
The experience had a lasting impact on how she saw the world and ultimately helped shape her plans for the future. “Building ramps and planting trees in the orchard felt so simple but they made such a huge difference to the communities we stayed in. The really changed my perspective on the world and has definitely influenced my next steps.”
Her growing interest in social inequality, development and geopolitics has led her towards Human Geography and an ambition to use what she learns to make a difference in the future.
Looking back, Eva believes one of the biggest changes during her years at Blackheath High has been in herself. She says, “My time at Blackheath has turned me from a shy and extremely nervous person into someone who isn’t afraid to voice their opinions and ask questions. I think a lot of that comes down to the relationships I’ve built, particularly in the Sixth Form – we’re a really close community.”
Eva also enjoyed the more independent style of Sixth Form learning, with smaller classes creating a seminar-like environment where questions, discussion and debate are actively encouraged. Just as important are the close relationships students build with their teachers. “The teachers at Blackheath High are truly some of the kindest and most caring people I have ever met. Each one of them will go out of their way to help us succeed in whatever we want to do.”
Looking to the future
Leaving the community she has grown up in will inevitably be bittersweet. Eva says “I’m going to miss the sense of community and the amazing friends and teachers I have at Blackheath, but I’m excited for the next steps and feel well prepared for life at university and beyond.”
From the nervous Year 3 pupil arriving for her first taster day to a confident young woman ready to study the global issues that fascinate her, Eva’s journey is a lovely example of what it means to find your own path at Blackheath High.

GCSE Results 2026
Blackheath High students celebrate outstanding GCSE result
Blackheath High School students are celebrating another exceptional set of GCSE results, with more than three quarters (77%) of all grades awarded at Grades 9-7 (equivalent to A**-A).
GCSE RESULTS
More than half (54%) of all grades were awarded at Grades 9-8, while more than nine in ten (92%) achieved Grades 9-6. The average GCSE grade across the cohort was an impressive 7.5.
Behind every grade is an individual story of hard work and determination – and today, there was plenty to celebrate. More than a third of students (36%) achieved Grades 9-7 across every subject, one in eight achieved straight Grades 9–8, and 71% of students received at least one of the highest possible Grade 9s.
The results continue Blackheath High’s strong trajectory in academic achievement, matching last year’s record-breaking results. The proportion of all grades awarded at Grade 9 has more than doubled since 2019, rising from 13% to 29% this year.
Girls excelling across STEM
STEM subjects delivered particularly strong results, with more than 90% of grades across Biology, Chemistry and Physics awarded at Grades 9–7. More than half of our Chemistry students (58%) achieved the highest Grade 9, while 68% of Physics grades were awarded at Grades 9–8. Our Statistics students also excelled, with 100% of grades awarded at Grades 9–7. Students take this GCSE a year early, in Year 10, completing the course in just one academic year – once more challenging persistent gender stereotypes around Mathematics and embodying what a girls’ school education is truly for: not just access to every subject, but the confidence to own it.
Excellence across the curriculum
Outstanding achievement extended far beyond STEM. In Drama, 100% of grades were awarded at Grades 9–8, while 91% of Geography grades achieved Grades 9–7, alongside 88% in Art, 84% in French and 81% in English Literature. Religious Studies also stood out, with nearly two thirds (64%) of grades awarded at the highest Grade 9.
This breadth of academic excellence is reflected in Blackheath High’s distinctive GCSE offer. In the first year of offering GCSE Psychology, 80% of grades were awarded at Grades 9–8, while both students studying Ancient Greek achieved Grade 8.
Natalie Argile, Head of Blackheath High School, said, “Walking through the school this morning and seeing these young women celebrating their results reminds me exactly why this job matters. Every single one of them has earned this moment.
“Behind these results are years of hard work and determination, alongside exceptional teaching. I am incredibly proud of these brilliant students, and enormously grateful to the staff who have taught, inspired and encouraged them throughout their GCSE years.
“At Blackheath High, we have always believed that when girls are known, supported and given the confidence to pursue their ambitions, they are capable of extraordinary things. Today is that belief made real. There is no single version of success here and that is precisely the point. These girls are all individuals, with their own passions, talents and ideas about where they want to go next. Today we celebrate how far they have come. The next chapter is entirely theirs.”
Ready for what comes next
The celebrations follow Blackheath High’s record-breaking A-level results last week, when 55% of grades were awarded at A*–A and 80% at A*–B, marking an exceptional year of academic achievement across the Senior School and Sixth Form.
For the majority of our Year 11 students, the next chapter will begin right here at Blackheath High Sixth Form. In September, they will be joined by a record number of students from other schools.
As Sixth Formers, students have the opportunity to deepen their academic interests while developing the skills and experiences that prepare them for life beyond school through leadership, co-curricular opportunities, work experience and our Futures programme. As part of the GDST, they also benefit from specialist opportunities extending far beyond the school, including GDST LEAD and the GDST Space Technology Diploma.
Mrs Argile added: “GCSE results day is an important milestone, but what excites me most is what comes next. These girls are curious, ambitious and ready to take on new challenges, and I cannot wait to see where their interests and talents take them during the next two years and beyond.”
Read about some of our fantastic students and their stories of success at Blackheath High School:
Charlotte joined Blackheath High in Year 7 from John Ball School after discovering the school through online events during the pandemic. Even virtually, she was impressed by the welcoming atmosphere and knew it was the right place to challenge herself and pursue her ambitions.
Following excellent GCSE results, Charlotte is delighted to be continuing her journey at Blackheath High Sixth Form, where she will study Physics, Maths and Chemistry alongside an EPQ. Looking further ahead, she hopes to pursue a career in mechanical or automotive engineering, potentially through a degree apprenticeship with a Formula One team.
Exploring every opportunity
Charlotte has embraced a huge range of opportunities throughout her time at Blackheath High. She has completed both Bronze and Silver Duke of Edinburgh’s Awards and plans to continue to Gold in Sixth Form. She also achieved a prestigious Gold CREST Award for a Year 9 research project, represented the school at the Interschool Cycling Championships at Herne Hill Velodrome, winning first place with her team, and enjoyed taking part in the annual Fashion Show as both a model and, the following year, a designer, creating a piece inspired by Greek mythology.
Determined to explore different career pathways, Charlotte completed work experience across engineering, healthcare and motorsport, including placements at a structural engineering firm, Gallions Reach Health Centre, Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the Red Bull Technology Campus.
From observing heart surgery to learning how a power-assisted steering rack is assembled, each placement gave her a valuable insight into different industries. It was her time at Red Bull, however, that has confirmed automotive engineering is the career she wants to pursue.
Reflecting on her time at Blackheath High, Charlotte says the confidence she has developed has been one of her greatest achievements. Awarded a Sixth Form Academic Scholarship and the Lucy Forrest Maths Award, she says an additional GCSE in Statistics strengthened her passion for maths and confirmed her ambition to study engineering. She believes the school’s supportive community helped her grow from a shy Year 7 pupil into someone who is confident to ask questions, share ideas and embrace new challenges.
“My friends and teachers are the main reason I wanted to stay on for Sixth Form. Blackheath High has given me the confidence to speak openly and without fear – something I know will be invaluable in my future career.”
Matilda joined Blackheath High Nursery in 2013 and has grown up in our close-knit school community. When the family was exploring Senior School options ahead of Matilda’s 11+ journey, they visited the Senior School Open Morning and were incredibly impressed with the girls who led them on tour – confident, friendly and warm. They knew this was somewhere that would prepare their daughter for a bright future,
Thanks to an incredible set of GCSE results, a bright future is exactly what Matilda has ahead of her. This September, Matilda will continue her journey at Blackheath High Sixth Form, where she plans to study Philosophy, Religion and Ethics, Government and Politics, and Economics, alongside an EPQ.
Embracing every opportunity
Matilda has embraced school life both in and beyond the classroom. As a Sports Scholar, she has represented the school in netball, hockey and cricket and captained the netball team. She has also achieved her Bronze and Silver Duke of Edinburgh’s Awards, completed a Gold CREST Award and Bronze LAMDA, played the drums, won the prestigious Greenman speaking competition and taken part in Model United Nations.
Leadership has been a constant throughout her time at Blackheath High. From serving as Head Girl in the Junior School and Form Captain throughout almost all of Senior School, to leading assemblies and supporting her peers, she credits the school with helping her develop the confidence and the voice to step forward and make a difference.
Ready for Sixth Form
Looking back on her time at Blackheath High so far, Matilda says some of her happiest memories include Duke of Edinburgh expeditions, hockey tours to Newcastle, netball trips to Condover and Disneyland, science practicals and PE and English lessons – all underpinned by spending time with her friends at break and lunchtime. She believes the opportunities she has been given have helped her develop confidence, resilience, teamwork and a strong work ethic.
With an eye on the future, she has completed work placements with the Metropolitan Police, local retailer Cheese at Turnpins and food campaigners School Food Matters.
She says: “I am really looking forward to so many different things about Sixth Form – studying subjects I am truly passionate about, having more independence and responsibility, and also to learning from really brilliant subject teachers.”
Millie joined Blackheath High in Year 7 from Gatehouse School after visiting for a Modern Foreign Languages event in Year 5. Inspired by the welcoming atmosphere and outstanding Languages department, she knew she had found the perfect place to nurture her love of languages.
Following an outstanding set of GCSE grades, Millie is excited to be moving into Blackheath High Sixth Form, where she plans to study Physics, Maths, French and German, alongside an EPQ. Looking further ahead, she hopes to combine her passions by studying Mechanical Engineering with German and French at university.
Beyond the classroom
Academic success has just been one part Millie’s Blackheath High story. A talented musician, she has been a member of Sinfonia, the Clara Schumann String Ensemble and Junior String Quartet since Year 7, and is currently working towards Grade 7 on both the violin and cello. Alongside music, Millie has completed her Silver LAMDA Award and both Bronze and Silver Duke of Edinburgh’s Awards, developing leadership, teamwork and resilience. She also credits opportunities such as the Greenman public speaking competition with helping her grow in confidence.
The spirit of adventure
One of the many gifts Blackheath High has given Millie is a love of travel and adventure. Among her favourite memories Geography fieldwork in Iceland and a Languages trip to Berlin. This summer, she is thrilled to be travelling to Nepal as part of a Blackheath High Global Action expedition with students from Norwich High School GDST. As well as trekking through Nepal’s breathtaking landscapes, students will work alongside local communities on a sustainability project to help improve access to clean drinking water.
Looking ahead to Sixth Form, Millie says: “I am really looking forward to this new chapter – Sixth Form is really different to the rest of the school, we get to be much more independent and organise our time ourselves. I am excited for the academic challenge too, and I feel like the school has prepared me really well for the move up – I had a Sixth Form taster day where I experienced a day as a BHS Sixth Former studying my chosen subjects, and we also got to speak in depth with the Head Student Team about Sixth Form life.”
